name: Elevation
description: A restrained elevation system for raised controls, floating surfaces, overlays, and dialogs.
rationale: Use elevation only to communicate spatial hierarchy, separation, or temporary layering. Keep the system intentionally small so shadows remain meaningful rather than decorative. Most static content should rely on spacing, contrast, borders, and surface color for hierarchy; shadows are reserved for elements that visually sit above surrounding content.
guidance: Use the lowest elevation level that clearly communicates the relationship. Use raised elevation for subtly lifted interactive or floating elements, overlay elevation for menus, popovers, dropdowns, and other temporary surfaces, and dialog elevation for modal surfaces that sit above the primary application layer. Avoid shadows on ordinary static cards, panels, and page sections unless elevation is necessary to communicate stacking. Prefer soft multi-layer shadows with low opacity over hard or highly visible shadows. Do not increase elevation merely to make an element appear more important; use hierarchy, typography, color, or spacing for emphasis instead.
notes: The system intentionally uses only three elevation levels. Raised is subtle enough for lightweight floating elements, overlay provides clearer separation for temporary surfaces, and dialog creates the strongest depth for modal interfaces. Additional elevation levels should only be introduced when a recurring spatial relationship cannot be represented clearly by these three.

tokens.name: shadow.raised
tokens.description: Subtle elevation for lightweight floating or raised elements that need gentle separation from the surrounding surface.

tokens.name: shadow.overlay
tokens.description: Medium elevation for dropdowns, menus, popovers, tooltips, and temporary floating surfaces.

tokens.name: shadow.dialog
tokens.description: Strongest standard elevation for dialogs, modals, and major temporary surfaces above the main application layer.
